messages:
Acme Ops (customer): Hey, we started seeing JSON parser errors in prod after you rolled rwd-model-3.0 last night. Our downstream ingestion fails with a JSONDecodeError. Happening for ~5% of requests, non-deterministic.

Acme Ops (customer): Sample request id: req_2026_11_03_4821. We call /v1/generate with structured_output=true and expect a top-level object like {\"answer\":..., \"sources\":[...]}.

Acme Ops (customer): Here's the raw response body we received (copied from logs):
```
{"_meta": {"model_version":"rwd-model-3.0","run_id":"abc123"}, "answer": "Foo", "sources": []}
```

Acme Ops (customer): Our parser expects no _meta key and chokes when additional fields appear inline; we get: JSONDecodeError + schema validation failure.

Jules (Support): Sorry about this — we're looking. Quick Qs: were these streaming responses or non-streaming? Did you set any response_schema / response_format params? Also can you paste the failing request payload (headers + body) for req_2026_11_03_4821?

Acme Ops (customer): Non-streaming. We just set structured_output=true (legacy flag). Body: `{\"prompt\":..., \"structured_output\":true, \"model\":\"rwd-model-3.0\", \"temperature\":0}`. Headers include x-request-id=req_2026_11_03_4821.

sre-bot: Detected correlated errors for model=rwd-model-3.0 across customer bucket acme-corp, rate ~4.7% over last hour. Logging trace ids attached.

Lina (Eng-ML): Thanks — I can reproduce locally using the same payload and model tag. Earlier model (rwd-model-2.9) returned: `{\"answer\":...,\"sources\":[...]}`. New model emits a small wrapper `_meta` or sometimes `confidence` fields at top-level depending on prompt. That will break strict validators. Suspect system prompt or generation head added a metadata return.

Lina (Eng-ML): Short repro (local run):
```bash
# curl to mimic client
curl -X POST https://inference/redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"model":"rwd-model-3.0","prompt":"<INSTRUCT>","structured_output":true,"temperature":0}'
# sample output
{"_meta":{"model_version":"rwd-model-3.0"},"answer":"Bar","confidence":0.92}
```

Alex (SRE): For immediate mitigation we can pin this customer to rwd-model-2.9 (traffic switch) or set their workspace to use the hosted "strict_json" response_format if available. Which would you prefer, @Maya?

Maya (Customer Success): Customer wants minimal disruption to production. If pinning model preserves behavior, do that now and we'll communicate. Also keep them in the A/B group for rollback window.

Jules (Support): I'm going to pin Acme's workspace to rwd-model-2.9 and open an internal incident. Will update here in a minute.

Jules (Support): action: pinned acme-corp -> rwd-model-2.9 (rolled back at 2026-11-03T21:07:12Z). Please confirm if errors stop.

Acme Ops (customer): Confirmed — error rate dropped to zero within minutes. Thanks.

Lina (Eng-ML): Root cause notes: model variant introduced optional metadata keys in the response head (likely from a new post-processing head used in some RLHF runs). Fix options: (1) remove metadata emission in postprocess stage (preferred), (2) add an operator-level sanitizer that strips unknown top-level keys when structured_output=true, (3) document and expose metadata via a namespaced key that downstreams can opt into.

Alex (SRE): We should avoid making runtime strip behavior by default unless explicitly enabled — could hide real regressions. Recommend short-term: sanitizer as an opt-in for affected customers + automatic rollback. Long-term: patch model.

Jules (Support): Filed INC-2451 to track eng fix and customer comms. Assigning to Lina (Eng-ML) for model patch and Alex for rollback playbook updates.

Lina (Eng-ML): Will prepare a model patch to remove the extra keys. ETA: ~48h for test + canary. I'll also add a small regression test in the structured-output eval harness to catch top-level key changes.

Jules (Support): Customer notified. Closing immediate support loop; keeping incident open for engineering fix.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2451 created by jules. Severity: P2. Linked logs and request ids: req_2026_11_03_4821 + traces.

Maya (Customer Success): Good work. Acme wants a short postmortem once fixed + a config knob so they can tolerate extra keys in future.

Lina (Eng-ML): Agreed — will add a 'allow_extra_top_level_keys' opt-in flag to the structured_output contract as part of the follow-up.

Jules (Support): Notes/Action items:
- rollback pinned for acme-corp -> rwd-model-2.9 (done)
- INC-2451 open (Lina, Alex owners)
- eng: model patch to remove metadata keys + add regression test (ETA 48h)
- product: consider opt-in sanitizer/contract (follow-up)

Acme Ops (customer): Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast triage. We'll keep an eye on the incident updates. :thumbsup:
